title: Upper bound on the shifted inner product
statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be binary words of length $n$, and let $\alpha \ge 0$. Suppose $d$ and $w$ are natural numbers for which the Hamming distance between $x$ and $y$ is at least $d$ and the Hamming weights of $x$ and $y$ are each at most $w$. Writing $\hat{x}^\alpha$ and $\hat{y}^\alpha$ for the corresponding shifted vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ — the $\pm 1$ embedding of the word minus $\alpha$ times the all-ones vector — their Euclidean inner product satisfies
\[
\langle \hat{x}^\alpha, \hat{y}^\alpha \rangle \;\le\; (n - 2d) + \alpha^2 n + 2\alpha\,(2w - n).
\]
hypotheses_covered: d ≤ Hamming distance between x and y
x, y are binary words of length n
